_format_note: PyTorch Vision training config. The cluster file owns node access; this file owns the container and the training workload; the sibling *_threshold.json owns per-sweep metric gates. Run with: cvs run pytorch_vision_single|pytorch_vision_distributed --cluster_file <cluster>.json --config_file <this>.json --html <out>.html --self-contained-html
_thresholds_comment: Gating is threshold-driven and requires enforce_thresholds=true. A threshold entry with kind=info always passes and records the value. Calibrate on the target filesystem and fabric before enforcing numeric limits.
_training_comment: training{} defines the workload. `workload` is the scorecard row id (W1 ResNet-50, W3 ViT-B/16) and is cross-checked against the result artifact. `distributed` must match the suite you invoke and the cluster node count. `run_mode` selects the profile (smoke|perf|train_5k|train_to_accuracy) and determines which rows are gated. `optimizer` is sgd or adamw; transformer backbones need adamw.
_sweeps_comment: training.sweeps[] are full training runs. Each `name` is also its threshold cell key, so encode every material dimension (topology, precision, microbatch, GA, data mode, rocAL device, augmentation) to stop a result being compared against the wrong gate. `label` is the compact id used in pytest rows and log directory names. training.enabled_sweep_list selects which names execute.

error_patterns.NCCL ERROR: NCCL ERROR|NCCL timeout|local work queue catastrophic error
error_patterns.GPU HW ERROR: HW Exception by GPU|GPU Hang|Uncorrectable error|GPU Reset
error_patterns.Python error: Traceback \(most recent call last\)|ModuleNotFoundError|Fatal Python error

_topology_comment: Node count comes from the cluster file, not this config: the sweep name encodes only per-device dimensions so the same file runs on 2N, 4N, or any larger topology. world_size and the effective global batch are derived as gpus_per_node x nodes at run time. training.scaling_baseline.images_per_sec_total should hold the matching single-node result.
